summary_status: Exploratory partial-identification study; no unique mechanism identified

references.method: Bonferroni over four group tests, McDiarmid bounded differences, finite-sample moment inversion

notes: A confidence set covers the exact grid candidate with >=95% theoretical probability only when every stated bound and sampling condition holds.
The set is a finite-grid set, not a continuous confidence region for all possible equations.
The true candidate parameter is deliberately on the pre-specified grid; this favours recovery.
The procedure has no access to true latent counts, qB, site effects or random transfer rates.
Correctness of the reference/natural envelope is not inferable from these count data alone.
Ordinary natural step changes and biased independent reference samples are analysed as misspecification stress tests.

exact_likelihood.oracle_assumption: The four true source probabilities Q per section are known exactly to the scorer.
exact_likelihood.rate: H11 step amplitude 0.30, D0, deterministic half-up rounding
exact_likelihood.natural_comparator: Multinomial with matched first-order means; no transformation
exact_likelihood.interpretation: Only a controlled higher-order diagnostic; flexible unknown natural distributions can remove separation.

identification_limit.statement: Independent B->W binomial thinning of a multinomial component and a natural-only multinomial with shifted category probabilities can be exactly observationally equivalent.
identification_limit.scope: Stochastic independent thinning only; NOT exact equality for deterministic half-up integer rounding.
identification_limit.consequence: Even a valid partial-identification confidence set may remain broad or contain H00 despite a true simulated transformation.
